There were no extra deposits, so the ending balance reflects the investment itself rather than additional money added along the way.

The ride was positive but uneven. The portfolio rose to $1,039 before its largest setback began on December 5, 2025. It then fell to $988 by March 30, 2026, a 4.8% drop from its earlier high. That was a real loss in the recorded balance during the decline, although the portfolio later recovered and finished at its highest recorded value of $1,086.

The market backdrop helps explain the rough patch. Reuters reported that the March selloff was driven by the conflict in the Middle East, higher oil prices, and renewed worries that inflation could keep interest rates higher for longer ([Reuters, March 20, 2026](https://www.reuters.com/business/wall-st-futures-slip-iran-war-rages-investors-dial-down-rate-cut-bets-2026-03-20/)). Later reporting described the same combination of war-related oil pressure and rate concerns weighing on stocks ([Reuters, March 24, 2026](https://www.reuters.com/business/us-stock-futures-dip-middle-east-uncertainty-tempers-relief-rally-2026-03-24/)). These events are a reasonable explanation for the market weakness during the drawdown, but they do not by themselves identify why each individual RSI trade occurred.

The broader market subsequently recovered. Reuters reported that the S&P 500 reached a record close in August as technology shares advanced and worries about rate increases eased ([Reuters, August 13, 2026](https://www.reuters.com/video/watch/idRW527713082026RP1/)). By the test's end, the strategy had earned 8.6% on its starting capital, bringing the portfolio to $1,086.

The meaningful tradeoff was versus simply holding the benchmark. The benchmark returned 16.9%, so the strategy finished 8.3 percentage points behind it. In everyday terms, the RSI approach delivered a gain while moving in and out of SPY, but staying with the benchmark for the whole window would have produced the larger result. The strategy's measured annualized volatility was 6.1%, with a Sharpe ratio of 1.4, but there is no comparable benchmark volatility in the test facts, so the results do not establish that the strategy was smoother than the benchmark."}
